correctness.rationale: The six-stage dissection is an exact identity in integer formal power series. The degree-1605 numerator has four equal mod-32 residue sections, each given by a degree-at-most-24 polynomial. A finite mod-8 Mahler certificate proves the exact Thue–Morse sixth-power reduction; dividing by unit-constant series yields the congruence at every nonnegative index. Legendre’s theorem and pairwise cancellation in the Thue–Morse word prove the iff classification on the four progressions and exact density 1/32 of their union. The supplied checker independently reconstructs all critical finite polynomial identities from formulas and also tests 32768 terms; the finite tests are not mistaken for an infinite proof.

Statement-level comparisons against indexed mathematics and accessible prior claims found no equivalent/stronger covering formula. This is best-knowledge priority, not an exhaustive search.

value.rationale: The original 2022/2023 paper poses explicit problems about three-square representability for color counts outside 2^j−1 and about interpretable modular laws. The case m=5 is the first odd count beyond m=3 not in the solved family. Four simple mod-32 Thue–Morse laws supply an infinite iff classification and a positive-density 1/32 obstruction subset, a structural advance beyond generic automaton existence and finite enumeration.
